claim: Norway spruce in the landscape: moderate to fast when young, about 23 m in 50 years.
section: Growth Rate: Moderate to fast, especially when young. (may grow to 75 feet in 50 years).

claim: Norway spruce is stiff when young, becoming more graceful with age.
section: Mature Shape: Pyramidal with branches that hang down. Stiff when young, becoming more graceful with age.

claim: Norway spruce plantation: growth in the first ten years after planting is slow; 8 to 11 years to reach a 1.8 to 2.1 m tree.
section: Growth during the first 10 years after field planting is relatively slow and 8 to 11 years are required to grow a 6-7 foot tree.

claim: Norway spruce reaches a 1.8 to 2.1 m tree within five years of field planting.
section: Growth during the first 10 years after field planting is relatively slow and 8 to 11 years are required to grow a 6-7 foot tree.

claim: Stump sprouts reach up to 0.9 m a year for the first three years.
section: Stump sprouts may grow as much as 3 ft per year during the first 3 years.

claim: Wild seedlings put down a deep taproot and the shoot stays small and shrubby for many years.
section: The shoot of natural seedlings often remains small and shrubby for many years, perhaps to accommodate development of deep roots.

claim: Open-grown Oregon white oak reaches 2.4 m in height at ten years of age.
section: Good potential for growth of this species is indicated by the following site characteristics: Top height on mature trees of at least 60 ft Sustained height growth of 1 to 2 ft per year for trees 10 to 30 years old Continuing diameter growth on mature trees.

claim: Oregon white oak typically grows 1 to 2 ft per year between ages 10 and 30.
section: Good potential for growth of this species is indicated by the following site characteristics: Top height on mature trees of at least 60 ft Sustained height growth of 1 to 2 ft per year for trees 10 to 30 years old Continuing diameter growth on mature trees.

claim: Oregon white oak height growth is usually under 0.3 m a year.
section: Growth of Oregon white oak is generally slow. Height growth is usually less than 1 ft per year and diameter growth is often 15 to 20 rings/in.
